blocking.title: G10 still passes when README.md or docs/REPORT.md shows a hand-edited figure: embedded_images misses CommonMark forms that GitHub renders
blocking.evidence: The review 3 B1 fix (c33bad4) says in docs/ARTIFACTS.md:84 that embedded_images finds embeds 'in every form a renderer shows'. Three classes of CommonMark that GitHub's own renderer (cmark-gfm, through its cmarkgfm Python binding) shows as images escape it; each snippet was rendered with cmark-gfm and passed to the clone's embedded_images. (1) One unclosed '![[' anywhere before an image makes _closing_bracket return None and the scan breaks (report.py:2676-2677), so every later Markdown image in the document goes unchecked: an invisible HTML comment '<!-- ![[ -->', a code span with '![[', or prose such as 'wiki links look like ![[page]] or ![[' before '![Pilot](img/copy.svg)' gives img src=img/copy.svg in cmark-gfm and [] from embedded_images. (2) Link reference definitions that LINK_DEF_RE (report.py:131-133, anchored at a line start, destination on the same line) does not see: inside a block quote ('> [pc]: img/copy.svg'), inside a list item ('- [pc]: ...', '1. [pc]: ...', '> - [pc]: ...'), or with the destination on the next line ('[pc]:' then 'img/copy.svg', or '<img/copy.svg>'). cmark-gfm renders '![Pilot][pc]' as the image; embedded_images returns []. (3) Decoy definitions: LINK_DEF_RE also matches lines the renderer does not treat as definitions (inside an HTML comment, a fenced code block, or a paragraph), and setdefault keeps the first one. With '<!--', '[pc]: figures/pilot.svg', '-->' before '![Pilot][pc]' and the real '[pc]: img/copy.svg' after it, cmark-gfm renders img/copy.svg while embedded_images reports figures/pilot.svg, a generated figure, so the check approves it (it fails open). End to end in a scratch clone of 526ae0d: docs/img/pilot-copy.svg is docs/figures/pilot.svg with the three 'Rule broken' bars and titles set to 0 (artifacts/pilot/opportunities.jsonl has 2 each for granite, qwen, and smollm). README.md:62's pilot image became '![Pilot: ...][pilot]' with '[pilot]:' and 'docs/img/pilot-copy.svg' on the next line, and docs/REPORT.md got '<!-- ![[ -->' under its title and '![Family pilot, per family ...](img/pilot-copy.svg)' after the results block; committed. cmark-gfm shows the copy in both documents. make claimcheck (CLAIMCHECK: PASS 167 claim(s) in 2 document(s)), make freshness (FRESHNESS: PASS 4 derivation(s), 125 live claim(s)), and make report-check (REPORT: CURRENT) pass, and tools/ship_check.py gate_g10 run on that clone prints 'G10 PASS make claimcheck ok; make freshness ok; make report-check ok' (gate_g13 also passes). A second commit using form (3) for README.md:62 also gives G10 PASS. Control: with the comment removed and the definition on one line, report-check prints 'REPORT: STALE (run make report): README.md embeds an image that make report does not generate: docs/img/pilot-copy.svg, docs/REPORT.md embeds an image that make report does not generate: img/pilot-copy.svg'. Rule 1 covers figures, so G10 passes while both documents show a figure with fabricated violation counts. tests/test_report.py test_embedded_images_finds_every_embedding_form covers none of these forms. This is the review 3 B1 class, re-raised with new forms and a new reproduction. Fix: collect images from what a reader sees, by rendering each document with a CommonMark and GFM implementation (cmark-gfm or markdown-it-py) and reading img, source, and the other embedding elements from the rendered HTML with an HTML parser, or fail closed on any reference anywhere in the raw text to an image file the build does not write; add each form above as a mutation test.

non_blocking: Canary coverage (D-055) stops at the template files. artifacts/bench/reference/*.log.json (every template's rules, reasons, detector parameters, and its compliant route's tool calls and file contents, including the six held-out E4 templates), artifacts/pilot/plans.jsonl and artifacts/pilot/compactions/ (pilot request text, scripted solutions, and full contexts), and src/halflife/data/probe_answers.yaml (a labeled dataset over every rule) carry no canary GUID: a search for 6ab2a05f-efff-4688-b98e-816aeac65e1a finds it only in the templates, docs/DATA.md, src/halflife/bench/__init__.py, and tests/test_bench.py. The templates meet rule 9 as D-055 scopes it, but a corpus filter keyed on the GUID keeps these copies, so README.md:29 ('so the templates can be filtered out of training corpora') holds for the files only. Consider a canary field in each artifact that embeds template content, re-banked by its script.

Mermaid charts escape G10. GitHub renders a mermaid code block as a figure, but claimcheck blanks fenced code (docs/CLAIMS.md:96 leaves numbers in code blocks to the reviewer) and report-check does not treat the block as an image. A scratch commit on 526ae0d that adds a mermaid 'pie showData' chart with "rule broken" : 0 and "rule kept" : 40 to README.md passed gate_g10 (the artifact has 6 of 40). No mermaid block in README.md or docs/REPORT.md holds a digit today (the README.md:69-82 flowchart has none). Treat mermaid blocks as figures: scan them as text, or fail on any digit in them.

README.md:65 says the audit caught bugs 'before any data existed', but E0 detector data was banked on 2026-10-23 (ef32e3e) and pilot sessions were running before the audit commit 68ef8e1 (2026-11-04); README.md:3 and :49 say 'before any confirmatory data', which is accurate. The same line ends 'Each fix is test-first and recorded (D-049, D-050)', but no D-050 fix is implemented at 526ae0d, and the interval rule that rejected about 8% of true nulls for H1 and H2b (D-050 item 1) is still the decision rule (docs/REPORT.md:75). Cite D-049 for the fixes and D-050 as decided.

README.md:27 says each review's blocking findings and their fixes are recorded in DECISIONS.md, but review 3's B1 (image forms) and B3 (README wording) have no DECISIONS.md entry; only B2 has one (D-055), and B3 is logged in CORRECTIONS.md. STATUS.md:23 and :43 say all three review 3 findings are fixed; this review's B1 shows the image-form fix is incomplete.

The re-banked bench records name a commit that does not hold their inputs: artifacts/bench/routes/*.json and artifacts/bench/reference/*.json record provenance git_sha b6ecb37, whose templates have no canary line, while their template_sha256 values are the post-canary hashes first committed in c33bad4. The bank ran in an uncommitted tree and halflife.bench.verify records no dirty flag, so rerunning the recorded command at the recorded SHA gives other template hashes. Record a dirty flag (as runner.run_provenance now does) or bank after committing the inputs.

artifacts/pilot/plans.jsonl keeps the pre-canary template hashes (D-055), and halflife.experiment.check_plans refuses all 3 banked pilot plans at 526ae0d ('pilot-unit-converter-0f426a29-s900000: template unit-converter changed since planning'). D-055 says no check compares the plans with the current files, but the run-time check does, so the pilot can no longer be rerun from its banked plans without regenerating them (identical apart from template_sha256, since plan randomization does not use the hash).

G6 trusts each compliant-route record's self-reported violations: 0 and tasks_passed (tools/ship_check.py:996-1002) and checks only the layout of the reference action log; it could rerun halflife.detect.detect_all on the banked reference logs offline. Rerun for this review: 0 violations across all 30 reference logs, and all 226 recorded span success values are true, so the property holds today.

G7 never checks that E1 rows use main-split templates read from the template files (tools/ship_check.py:1339-1412); only G9 excludes held-out templates. Brief sections 5 and 10.2 step 4 keep the pilot templates and seeds out of E1; designs/e1.yaml (split main, seed_base 100000) and designs/pilot.yaml (split pilot, seed_base 900000) are disjoint today. Defense in depth, since G7 cannot pass yet.

src/halflife/analysis.py:125-127 says the analysis drops procedure-rule opportunities whose span a cap cut, but nothing reads span_end yet (only analysis.py and tests mention it); D-050 item 5 is in on the harness side only, so use the future tense until the exclusion lands. runner.run_provenance (src/halflife/runner.py:111) sets git_dirty from src/ and designs/ only, so a changed tools/, budget.toml, or uv.lock is not flagged.

G12 and make review trust the self-reported reviewer field ('subagent' or 'headless'), so nothing offline shows that the main session did not write artifacts/review/latest.json. This is inherent offline; docs/ARTIFACTS.md could say that authorship rests on the commit record.

Counts still written as words: docs/REPORT.md:84 says Llama-3.2-3B 'ran no pilot session', and README.md:45 says 'two or three rules drawn from four types' (design facts; 19 templates have two rules and 11 have three). Claimcheck cannot see them, and they would not follow a change. The README.md:45 template count and the README.md:58 counts flagged by review 3 are now claims.

G11 trusts each artifact's self-declared 'confirmatory' flag (src/halflife/integrity/prereg.py:256-260), and G8/G9 (tools/ship_check.py:1476-1648) never require a preregistration link for E3/E4 even though designs/e3.yaml and designs/e4.yaml declare confirmatory: true. The run tool refuses confirmatory plans without --prereg (src/halflife/experiment.py:543-553), so this is defense in depth; consider deriving confirmatory status from the committed design.

Probes advance the main run's seed counter (src/halflife/agent.py:258-260, temperature 0.7), so main-run sampling depends on how many probes ran. Probe content never enters the main context, and probes run in every E1 condition, so there is no bias between arms, but 'never contaminate the main run' holds for content only, and README.md:48 still says the probes 'never touch the main run'; say so, or give probes their own seed stream.
G5 probe leakage is recomputed only from per-session leak flags the harness wrote (src/halflife/experiment.py:445). Main-run contexts are not banked, so leakage cannot be re-derived from artifacts/.

E0 detector validation (artifacts/e0/detector_validation.json, git_sha 26a388f, 2026-10-23) predates the subject-env sandbox change (f3db2ec) and the template test-run pattern change (D-036). src/halflife/detect.py has not changed since E0 (no later commit touches it), but the current sandbox has not been re-validated by E0; note it in the E1 preregistration or re-run E0.

docs/REPORT.md:75 reports a simulation result (the score test 'held its nominal level where a plain cluster-robust sandwich rejected too often') with no banked artifact cited, and README.md:49 ('score tests calibrated on synthetic nulls') rests on it. docs/REPORT.md:53 ('the forced indices first drawn fell after most sessions had ended') is a dry-run observation with no artifact. Bank and cite both, or mark them unbanked.

Probe-scorer keyword groups were tuned on dev-split answers that cover the held-out E4 templates' rules too (src/halflife/data/probe_answers.yaml, D-038). This is not leakage into E4 outcomes, but the held-out templates are not unseen by instrument tuning; state it in the E4 preregistration.

RQ1 asks for half-life per agent, model, and constraint type. src/halflife/e1_analysis.py computes half-life per family only, and G7 checks it per family; D-050 item 4 calls per-rule-type half-lives exploratory. Settle the per-type estimand in prereg/0001-e1.md.

make freshness accepts 'raw' primary artifacts on the strength of a self-reported provenance block (command and git_sha; src/halflife/integrity/freshness.py docstring). That is inherent offline, but docs/CLAIMS.md should say that raw-artifact authenticity is not verified.
